# v0.8.7 human-scale FASTA ingestion benchmark

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

This benchmark measures the launch-screen delay and first self-plot delay separately.
It compares the preserved v0.8.6 eager reader with the v0.8.7 eager and indexed paths;
it is not a scientific-estimator accuracy benchmark.

## Fixture and host

* One FASTA record, 101,161,492 bases.
* Plain FASTA: 102,426,018 bytes.
* BGZF FASTA: 31,179,430 bytes.
* Plain index set: FASTA plus 24-byte FAI.
* BGZF index set: BGZF plus 24-byte FAI and 25,128-byte GZI.
* Chromium 151.0.7922.34 through Playwright, headless.
* Apple M1 Pro, 10 logical CPUs, 32 GiB memory, macOS arm64.
* Node 25.9.0.

Each case ran once for warmup and three times for measurement. Every measured run used
a fresh browser context and page within the same browser process. The landing timer
starts immediately before setting the browser file input and ends when **Explore** is
visible and enabled. The plot timer starts immediately before selecting **Explore** and
ends when the visible status begins with **Ready**. The timeout was 300 seconds.

## Results

| Input path | Median landing | Median first plot | Median total | Measured runs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| v0.8.6 eager plain baseline | 801.46 ms | 6,315.73 ms | 7,116.25 ms | 3/3 passed |
| v0.8.7 eager plain | 800.05 ms | 6,338.31 ms | 7,138.36 ms | 3/3 passed |
| v0.8.6 eager BGZF baseline | 1,306.25 ms | 6,325.33 ms | 7,634.53 ms | 3/3 passed |
| v0.8.7 eager BGZF | 1,304.00 ms | 6,795.25 ms | 8,124.02 ms | 3/3 passed |
| v0.8.7 indexed plain plus FAI | 31.66 ms | 7,259.70 ms | 7,291.74 ms | 3/3 passed |
| v0.8.7 indexed BGZF plus FAI/GZI | 31.78 ms | 7,369.24 ms | 7,400.37 ms | 3/3 passed |

All 12 measured v0.8.7 runs completed with no captured page or console error. Relative
to v0.8.6, v0.8.7 eager landing time changed by less than 0.2% for both encodings.
Indexed landing was 96.05% lower for plain FASTA and 97.57% lower for BGZF, equivalent
to 25.31-fold and 41.11-fold improvements.

Because the fixture has only one record and the first plot selects it, indexed loading
must perform the deferred record work immediately after **Explore**. Total time is
therefore similar: indexed plain was 2.47% above the v0.8.6 total, while indexed BGZF
was 3.07% below it. The v0.8.7 eager BGZF plot median was 7.43% above the baseline in
this small sample; its three plot measurements ranged from 6,551 to 6,851 ms, so the
observation is retained without a causal claim.

One additional indexed run captured resource reporting after the first plot. Plain
FAI input reported **Memory ~108.5 MiB** and BGZF FAI/GZI reported **Memory ~108.4
MiB**; both received the resource-plan action `admit`. Chromium's JavaScript heap
snapshot was 15.2 MB used for plain and 17.1 MB for BGZF. These figures are a
single-run operational sample, not peak process memory.

## Interpretation

The index fast path addresses the user-visible **Checking input.fa** pause by making
record metadata available without reading and packing every sequence. It does not make
the selected chromosome's scientific computation free. On a multi-record genome,
records that are never selected are never loaded, which is the intended reduction in
total input work and retained packed-sequence memory.
